source.title: Complexity Scaling Laws for Neural Models using Combinatorial Optimization
source.authors: Lowell Weissman; Michael Krumdick; A. Abbott

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling experiments to TSP models trained with reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning, and reports test-loss trends in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper's main results on TSP suboptimality, problem-complexity scaling, and local search are not results on the loss behavior named by the claim versions and are not included as rows. Results cited from other studies are also excluded. The included loss results concern TSP models, not language-model pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study trains Transformer pointer networks on 2D 20-node TSP with PPO and SFT at 12 model sizes. It fits power laws of test loss and suboptimality against parameters and compute. This is a new setting (combinatorial optimization, RL and supervised fine-tuning) for whether the scaling-law power-law form holds beyond text pretraining (V5). It does not study language models, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 as worded are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right; it understates the headline. The main result is that TSP suboptimality power-decays smoothly with parameters and compute for both RL and SFT. SFT is more compute-efficient, and optimal model size grows as a power of compute, as in other domains. Suboptimality also grows predictably with node count and spatial dimension for fixed-size models, mirrored by local search. The loss results (SFT NLL and critic loss power-decay; PPO actor loss zero-centered as expected) are secondary findings in Appendix C.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Transformer pointer networks on TSP, trained with PPO or one-epoch SFT, and examines TSP test losses rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss behavior differs by objective: SFT NLL and PPO critic loss show smooth power decay, while PPO actor mean loss has no obvious trend. The paper also reports that limited training can produce trend breakdown in larger experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: With model size fixed, TSP suboptimality follows power growth in node count (α≈1.86 RL, 1.69 SFT). It follows bounded exponential-decay growth in spatial dimension. SFT NLL loss decays exponentially with node count and does not track task performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-capacity model performance scales predictably with problem complexity (solution/representation space size).

fits_no_version.finding: The standard deviation of all loss components, including the PPO actor loss, power-decays with parameters and compute (Fig. 10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss variance follows scaling laws even when mean loss does not.

record.problems: Loss rows are described qualitatively rather than with fitted loss exponents or uncertainty estimates in the text. The study is on TSP rather than language modeling. The authors also note limited compute and single-seed training per model scale, limiting precision of some scaling comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the included loss-scaling results. TSP complexity-scaling losses and loss standard-deviation analyses are not rows for the versions tested here because they do not measure the mean held-out pretraining-loss behavior named by those versions.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out pretraining loss is measured.
No extrapolation from small to much larger runs. The authors say optimal-model-size extrapolation would be imprecise.
No LM parameter/token allocation. The TSP optimal-model-size vs compute fit (N∝C^0.82 RL, C^0.66 SFT) varies model size only, not tokens.
Only width is scaled. Depth/width shape effects at fixed parameter count are assumed from Kaplan, not tested.
Image/video models, repeated data and transfer are not tested. Only TSP with PPO and one-epoch SFT, over roughly 6e4 to 1.7e6 parameters (fitted range).
No downstream-task predictability from LM scale or loss.
No comparison of LM fitting choices. Trend breaks are attributed to insufficient training, not to fit choices.

missing.what: Suboptimality power laws vs parameters (α=0.582 RL, 0.712 SFT) and vs compute frontier (α=0.439 RL, 0.555 SFT), with leave-one-out SDs of about 0.011–0.015
Optimal model size vs compute: N∝C^0.816 (RL) and C^0.658 (SFT), with LOO SDs of about 0.064–0.071. The authors say these align with language, image and RL values.
SFT critic loss (predicting optimal tour length) also power-decays with parameters and compute
Larger models (up to ~5.9e6 params) fall off trend. The authors attribute this to insufficient training, not a true bend.

record.verdict_notes: The PPO actor-loss limits_scope label is removed: that objective is zero-centered by construction, and the authors say its lack of trend is expected. Fits come from single seeds per size over less than 1.5 orders of magnitude of parameters. Loss fit constants are only in the code repository.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test held-out pretraining loss of language models as parameters, tokens, or compute scale.
It does not test whether small-run language-model loss fits predict much larger language-model runs.
It reports a TSP optimal-model-size versus compute fit, but does not test language-model parameter-and-token allocation at fixed compute or compare token and parameter growth rates.
The study does not vary depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count to test their effects on loss.
The reported extension is to TSP models and RL/SFT losses; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer in language models, or other modalities.
The study does not test predictability of downstream-task performance from pretraining loss or language-model scale.

Although the paper discusses fit sensitivity and trend breaks for TSP performance, it does not test whether language-model loss exponents or the language-model compute-optimal parameter/token split depend on setup or fitting choices.

relationships.condition: TSP SFT next-node NLL and RL critic loss vs parameters and compute-efficient frontier, for models that converged to trend (~6e4 to 1.7e6 params)
relationships.reason: Appendix C.2/Fig. 9 reports smooth power decay of SFT NLL and PPO critic loss with parameters and compute (r1–r4). Suboptimality also power-decays (Table 1, from text).
relationships.display_finding: Supervised next-node NLL and PPO critic loss decayed smoothly as power laws with parameters and compute, while suboptimality also showed power-law decay.
